title: the release guard's speed case holds on any runner
desiredOutcome: guard-release's case for a long run of quoted -C operands proves the grading does not grow faster than the command does, by a measure independent of the machine's speed, so it is green on windows-latest and still red against the pre-fix behaviour

findings.issue: gw15, the sibling case of the same backtracking fix in guard-history-rewrite, still asserts an absolute wall-clock bound (_elapsed < 0.05) on a run of quoted -C operands, so a slow runner can turn it red the way gr60 went red; the fix was applied to one instance of the class.
findings.resolution: fixed in P98.2-yie (48a9aabc): Rewrite gw15 as gr60 now is - an interleaved min-of-N ratio between two operand counts, an unresolved timing failing, red-first against the code before the fix - and sweep the suites for any other absolute wall-clock bound.

findings.issue: The comment says a quadratic re-scan lands as far above the bound as the linear reading lands below, which holds only when the quadratic's per-operand cost is comparable to the call's fixed cost; a measured quadratic mutation gave 6.95-7.21 against the bound of 6.
findings.resolution: fixed in P98.2-yie (48a9aabc): Say what the bound guarantees: red against backtracking by orders of magnitude, and against a quadratic only when its per-operand cost is comparable to the call's fixed cost.

review.outcome: One review round: one med (gw15, the same wall-clock class) and one low (gr60's comment overclaimed a quadratic guarantee), both resolved by P98.2 in 48a9aabc, plus gr60's label corrected.
